{{Short description|Construction for categories}}
{{Other uses|Twisted diagonal (disambiguation)}}{{One source|date=May 2025}}
In [[category theory]] in [[mathematics]], the '''twisted diagonal''' of a [[Category (mathematics)|category]] (also called the '''twisted arrow category'''), which makes the morphisms of a category into the objects of a new category, whose morphisms are then pairs of morphisms connecting domain and codomain with the twist coming from them being in opposite directions. It can be constructed as the [[category of elements]] of the [[Hom functor]], which makes the twist come from the fact that it is [[Contravariant functor|contravariant]] in the first entry and [[Covariant functor|covariant]] in the second entry. It can be generalized to the [[Twisted diagonal (simplicial sets)|twisted diagonal of a simplicial set]] to which it corresponds under the [[Nerve (category theory)|nerve]] construction.

== Definition ==
For a category <math>\mathcal{C}</math>, its ''twisted diagonal'' <math>\operatorname{Tw}(\mathcal{C})</math> is a category, whose objects are its arrows:

: <math>\operatorname{Ob}(\operatorname{Tw}(\mathcal{C}))
=\operatorname{Ar}(\mathcal{C})</math>

and for which the morphisms between two such objects <math>f\colon A\rightarrow B</math> and <math>g\colon X\rightarrow Y</math> are the pairs <math>p\colon X\rightarrow A</math> and <math>q\colon B\rightarrow Y</math> of morphisms in <math>\mathcal{C}</math> so that <math>g=q\circ f\circ p</math>,<ref>Kerodon, [https://kerodon.net/tag/00AZ Construction 8.1.0.1.]</ref> then we get a commutative diagram

[[File:Twisted diagonal.svg]]

If <math>[1]</math> denotes the category <math>0\rightarrow 1</math> with two objects and one non-trivial morphism (with the notation taken from the [[simplex category]]), then the twisted arrow category <math>\operatorname{Tw}(\mathcal{C})</math> is ''not'' the [[functor category]] <math>\mathbf{Fun}([1],\mathcal{C})</math> since the morphisms between the domains is reversed. An alternative definition is as the [[category of elements]] of the [[Hom functor]]:

: <math>\operatorname{Tw}(\mathcal{C})
:=\operatorname{El}(\operatorname{Hom}_\mathcal{C}).</math>

There is a canonical functor:

: <math>\operatorname{Tw}(\mathcal{C})\rightarrow\mathcal{C}^\mathrm{op}\times\mathcal{C},(f\colon X\rightarrow Y)\mapsto(X,Y).</math>

== Properties ==

* Under the [[Nerve (category theory)|nerve]], the twisted diagonal of categories corresponds to the twisted diagonal of simplicial sets. For a category <math>\mathcal{C}</math>, one has:<ref name=":16">Kerodon, [https://kerodon.net/tag/03JN Proposition 8.1.1.10.]</ref>
*: <math>N\operatorname{Tw}(\mathcal{C})
=\operatorname{Tw}(N\mathcal{C}).</math>

* Slice and coslice categories arise through pullbacks from the twisted arrow category. For a category <math>\mathcal{C}</math>, one has:<ref>Kerodon, [https://kerodon.net/tag/03JE Remark 8.1.0.6.]</ref>
*: <math>X\backslash\mathcal{C}
\cong\{X\}\times_{\mathcal{C}^\mathrm{op}}\operatorname{Tw}(\mathcal{C}),</math>
*: <math>\mathcal{C}/X
\cong\operatorname{Tw}(\mathcal{C})\times_\mathcal{C}\{X\}.</math>
